$comment: Written by scripts/changelog.mjs from each game's GitHub Pages deploys. Summaries may be edited by hand: an update already here is never rewritten.

updates.summary: Blade Hymn launches in the browser as a sword-fighting platformer with three hand-crafted stages and three bosses. Dash combos and per-stage speedrun leaderboards are included, with a fixed timing clock so runs are fair to compare.

commits.text: Exact visual parity with the original pygame renderer

updates.summary: Graphics now match the original desktop version more closely, with sprites and scenery drawn at the same pixel positions as before.

commits.text: Rewrite the browser port as a pixel-exact translation of the original
Fit the page to the games frame and credit Eason's game as a port

updates.summary: The game now runs as a faithful translation of the original Blade Hymn, so movement and combat should feel closer to the desktop version. The page layout changed: the game fills the frame with a slim top strip for the speedrun clock, Speedruns, Keys, Credits and Fullscreen, and credits moved into their own panel.

BOP launches as a free browser physics brawler where you choose up to three of 29 wild abilities, cling to every side of floating terrain and knock friends off it. It supports online multiplayer for four, couch play on one screen, and practice bots across 15 arenas.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

commits.text: Tighten fidelity to the reference brawler

updates.summary: Four arenas no longer kill players on the first frame at spawn, and free-floating terrain no longer slowly sinks out of the world under a standing player.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

commits.text: Align match flow and refresh UI

updates.summary: The match flow has been tidied up and the interface refreshed.

commits.text: Add screen-relative surface controls

updates.summary: Surface controls now work relative to the screen, so the directions you press match what you see while clinging to terrain.

commits.text: Humanize practice bots

updates.summary: Practice bots move and fight more like human players.

commits.text: Stabilize practice rounds and grapple

updates.summary: Practice rounds against bots run more consistently, and the grapple holds steadier during a round.

commits.text: Synchronize multiplayer snapshots

updates.summary: Online matches now stay in sync between players, so positions and hits line up more reliably during multiplayer rounds.

commits.text: Smooth multiplayer motion

updates.summary: Multiplayer movement looks smoother for players online.

commits.text: Expire stale lobby listings

updates.summary: Stale lobby listings now disappear from the room browser after a while, so the list shows rooms that are actually open.

commits.text: Repair core gameplay systems

updates.summary: Core gameplay systems have been repaired, so matches should play as intended.

commits.text: Support protected live smoke tests

updates.summary: Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

updates.summary: Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

Show room region and live ping, follow room moves
Hide snapshot delay with an adaptive clock and delay-matched correction
Never draw remote bodies less than 100 ms behind the fastest path

updates.summary: Online rooms now show their region and your live ping in the room list, waiting room and HUD, with the ping coloured from 120 and 200 ms. When a group spread across regions starts a match, the room can move to a shard in a fairer region, and you reconnect automatically. Remote players are drawn with a smoother, adaptive delay, so motion on a steady connection looks less jumpy.

commits.text: Dev join, admins can join any lobby, even mid-match

updates.summary: Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

Raster smoke, black holes and bubbles as dithered pixels
Cache platform rasters and harden only the region each layer covers

updates.summary: The whole game now draws in a pixel art style, with bops shown as slimes that settle onto the surface they cling to. Smoke, black holes and bubbles are drawn as dithered pixels to match, and menus use a new paper and ink look with a pixel font.

commits.text: Middle click fires ability three instead of autoscrolling

updates.summary: Middle click now fires your third ability instead of starting the browser's autoscroll.

A free browser platformer with 46 hand-picked rooms across 14 chapters, precision movement including dashes, wall climbing and wave dashes, collectibles, achievements, and touch controls. The soundtrack and effects are synthesized in the browser with WebAudio.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

commits.text: Complete overhaul of all 46 curated room designs with authentic architecture and mechanics

updates.summary: All 46 rooms have been redesigned with new layouts and mechanics across the chapters.

commits.text: Enable arrow keys and enter keyboard navigation across all UI screens

updates.summary: Menus and screens can now be navigated with the arrow keys and Enter.

ROOK & ROLL launches as a free pixel-art chess game in the browser. Play nine computer opponents from beginner to full-strength Stockfish, with hints and takebacks, explore any position with the engine, and review your games move by move with accuracy scores.

commits.text: Show captured black pieces on a light chip

updates.summary: Captured black pieces now appear on a light chip, so they are easier to see.

commits.text: Rated puzzles and Puzzle Rush from the Lichess database

updates.summary: New rated puzzles drawn from about 5,000 positions, sorted into 26 rating bands and matched near your own rating. Each puzzle comes with hints, solution playback, a handoff to analysis, and themes shown afterward. Puzzle Rush is also new: solve as many as you can in three minutes, with three strikes ending the run.

commits.text: Online play with quick matches, friend links and ratings
Share friend games as ?game= links so they survive the hub frame

updates.summary: Online play is new: quick matches against other players, friend games through a shareable link, and rated games with ratings tracked by category. Clocks run on the server, with flag-fall and draw offers, claims and rematches supported. Friend links now open the game directly instead of the home screen.

Garden Defenders 2 launches as a free browser lane-defense tower defense game with five worlds of eight levels each, plus an endless mode for every world. It includes 20 plants, 15 zombie types, boss fights, and can be installed as a web app.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

A new game mode, GD 2.5: Remixed, is selectable from the title screen. It adds five world gimmicks such as tombstones, water gaps, minecart rails, freezing wind and power tiles, plus boss fights with world mechanics, star objectives, conveyor, Last Stand and locked level types, puzzle levels, three new plants and two new zombies.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

FART TOGETHER is a free co-op pixel-art raft game for 1 to 4 players. Hippos ride a round raft down procedurally generated sky flumes, steering by farting from their own share of the rim past spike walls, hammers and open drops.

Touch controls for phones and tablets. A floating stick on the left half of the screen walks your hippo around the rim, a FART button on the right is held to fart, and a pause button opens the menu. They appear only while playing on a touch device and work in solo and online games.

Courses are harder, with narrower channels on higher difficulties and new hazards: windmills, spinning hoops, wheels, stampers that crush you, spiked logs and floor holes. Doors and the hammer block are now spiked, and moving obstacles that stand alone must be timed.

Spiked walls now pop the raft, which bursts and respawns after a short pause, while windmill arms and bumpers only push it. Hammers swing slower, windmills no longer sit beside spike walls, and the course generation is harder overall.

The Play online screen now has a lobby browser that lists public rafts, refreshing every few seconds. Hosts can give their raft a name or make it private. Online joins no longer fail when the page is opened over plain http, because the site now redirects to https.
Water now spills over the open edge of a flume instead of pooling behind the lip.
Your own hippo now responds immediately to your inputs when playing online, so steering feels less laggy. Online play also shows a ping readout for each seat in the HUD.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
Each raft now shows its region and ping in the waiting room and during play. Mixed groups are moved to a fairer region when a match starts, and a raft that was moved is followed automatically.

When a player leaves mid-run, by button or by closing the tab, the raft re-splits between the crew that remains instead of keeping an empty seat. A dropped connection now removes that player after a 10 second grace period.

Players can now chat with a one-line box opened by Enter or T, and the line appears as a speech bubble over their hippo for a few seconds. Press E to pick one of six quick emotes (STOP, GO, LEFT, RIGHT, LOOK OUT, NICE!), shown over the hippo, and touch controls get buttons for chat and emotes.

Spectate buttons appear next to Join on every raft row and the join-by-code card, so you can watch any raft, full or private, without taking a seat. Spectators see the run, the waiting room and crew chat bubbles, and can take a free seat from the waiting room with Join raft. Opening a link with ?watch=CODE drops you straight into spectating that raft.
Local co-op on the title screen lets two players share one keyboard offline, with optional bots. In an online lobby, a second player can join from the same page using '+ Player 2 on this keyboard'.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
With two hippos, left and right now move each hippo around the raft as expected instead of leaving them stuck in the middle.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
ISUCK launches as a free browser roguelike with seeded floors, 732 collectibles, 34 playable characters, alternate paths, 208 enemies and 80 bosses.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

updates.summary: Rooms now connect properly and the gameplay view fits the window.

commits.text: Track room transitions in run state

Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

commits.text: Preserve full gameplay viewport at any display size

updates.summary: The gameplay view now fills the full play area at any screen size.

Playing the game brings a new HUD layout with a streak strip, a boss card before boss fights, a full map, sliding room transitions and ink-outlined visuals. Enemies, bosses, the protagonist and 34 characters have new original artwork, and in-game characters have bigger heads.

ONE WORLD launches as a shared anarchy survival world where every signed-in player joins the same map under their games.andrenijman.com username. A private local-world option and consent-based teleport requests are also available.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
Joining the shared world no longer fails with an expired or invalid join ticket error (401) when the game takes a while to connect after clicking the join button.
The main menu now shows a "Fix this" link when joining is blocked by a sign-in problem, so you can go straight to resolving it.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
Clicking join no longer nests the game inside extra copies of the site frame, so the game stays at full size when you rejoin.
Loading no longer hangs at "Preparing textures" or fails with asset load errors, for both shared and local worlds.
Sound effects and audio now play in the game, which were silent before.
Holding Shift now sprints, and C toggles crouch. The inventory can be clicked on touch devices that also have a mouse or keyboard.

Touch controls now follow the input device you are actually using. In auto mode, the first mouse or touch input decides the control layout, so switching from touch to a mouse on a touch laptop goes back to desktop controls. The old always-show touch controls setting is migrated to the new mode setting.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

Memory Burn is a free browser wave-survival shooter, solo or online co-op for up to four players. You fight 15 contracts across seven cyberpunk districts, spend eddies in a back-alley market between waves, face three named bosses, and then continue into an endless Afterburn mode.

commits.text: Add synthesized sound effects, a procedural soundtrack and volume settings

updates.summary: Sound effects and music are added throughout the game, with a soundtrack that changes by screen, district, boss and ending, plus ambient beds and dialogue voices. A new volume settings panel lets you adjust Master, Music and Sound Effects levels.

commits.text: Leave bought shop slots empty until the next market or a reroute

updates.summary: Bought cards in the back-alley market now leave their slot marked SOLD instead of refilling right away, and the slot stays empty until the next wave's market or a Reroute. Locked cards can no longer be bought again once purchased.

commits.text: Add online co-op for up to four players with its own Cloudflare relay
Rebind a reconnecting guest's runner and default to the relay domain
Flag a quiet host, drop a dead host socket, and lock the spectator market
Keep per-frame player fields out of co-op player sheets
Predict a co-op guest's own runner

updates.summary: Online co-op now supports up to four players, with one host running the game and guests joining by code. Guests see the host's game state and their own runner moves smoothly between updates. A guest who drops and rejoins keeps their runner and run progress, and guests see 'Host not responding' when updates stop for a few seconds.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

OVERPOP launches as a free round-based tower defense game with 25 woodland-critter towers, each with three-branch upgrade trees, across 100 rounds and 16 maps. Heroes level up, paragons unlock, and eleven game modes are included, with the game installable as an app and playable offline.

commits.text: Persist balloon speedMul; give on-canvas panels first refusal on a tap

updates.summary: Saves made while a balloon is slowed now reload it at its slowed speed instead of full speed. Taps on on-screen panels now take priority over the game canvas underneath them.

updates.summary: The upgrade tree button now sits on each tower card, so you can open a tower's upgrade tree without moving the pointer off the card. The tree is also sized to fit its text.

updates.summary: The one-life modes Purist, Grim, Rampart and Relentless now start with exactly one life instead of receiving the extra starting life bonus. Ordinary runs keep their bonus lives.

commits.text: Continue victories past the final round

updates.summary: After winning a game, players can now continue past the final round in freeplay on the same board without starting over.

updates.summary: Rounds that end with a lethal leak no longer award completion credit or rewards. Bosses no longer appear behind the results screen or carry into freeplay after the final round is won.

commits.text: Defer reload while a victory still offers freeplay

updates.summary: A page refresh from a game update no longer interrupts the victory screen before you pick FREEPLAY, so your winning board is kept.

updates.summary: On expedition result screens, ENTER now does what the footer hint says, so pressing it continues, completes, starts freeplay or retries depending on the screen. Previously ENTER did nothing there.

updates.summary: A won daily challenge no longer keeps running into freeplay, so its results are no longer recorded a second time.

commits.text: Restore the active daily challenge for reloaded runs

updates.summary: Daily challenge runs now keep their daily record and streak when you reload and resume a run.

commits.text: Replay a finished daily with its challenge seed and rules

updates.summary: Replaying a finished daily challenge now uses its original seed and rules, so the map and conditions match the day it was played.

commits.text: Replay a finished trial with its authored rules

updates.summary: Replaying a finished trial now starts with the rules it was authored with.

commits.text: Gate upgrades behind per-type tower XP

updates.summary: Tower upgrades now unlock as each tower type gains experience from use, so upgrades are earned per tower type rather than available right away.
The game is no longer installable as an app and no longer works offline in the browser.

commits.text: XP now only comes from popping, not from spending money

updates.summary: Hero XP now comes only from popping enemies, no longer from spending money.

commits.text: Distribute each round XP pool proportionally to money invested per tower

updates.summary: Round XP is now shared among your towers in proportion to the money you put into each one, so towers you invested more in earn a bigger share of the XP.

commits.text: Blend round pool 50/50 between money invested and tower pops

updates.summary: Round pools now blend money invested and tower pops evenly, so the mix of rounds you face reflects both how much you spend and how many pops you have to clear.

commits.text: Tower menu shows lifetime XP per tower and upgrade lock state

updates.summary: The tower menu now shows each tower's lifetime XP. It also shows whether each upgrade is locked.

updates.summary: The title screen now has a dedicated TOWERS menu for browsing the critter towers.

updates.summary: The Legends entry screen now has a button to start a new run.

commits.text: Add Starter Party picker and polish Legends results screen

updates.summary: A Starter Party picker lets you choose your opening towers before a run. The Legends results screen has been polished.

Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

Medium difficulty keeps its standard tuning through the Wraith rounds, so those waves play as they did before.

updates.summary: Stage bosses are now real encounters, with a boss preview on the board screen and a boss objective in the pause menu. Campaigns start with a party of two random towers (up to four) that deploy automatically at battle start alongside your hero. Chests offer three unowned artifacts to choose from, and campfire tiles let you rest to heal 25% of starting lives. The trophy store now opens from the title screen instead of returning to the title, and the legends screen has been rearranged so its artifacts and heroes fit on the field.

Rasists is a free 3D browser racing game where every race runs on a new procedurally generated track. Play online in rooms with friends, solo events against AI rivals, or time trials with ghost replays, and unlock, paint and upgrade cars in your garage.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

Cars grip better and accelerate faster, with a higher top speed and stronger brakes. The handbrake is gentler and a stability assist stops most spins, so corners no longer need heavy braking. Solo races now stay in step with your inputs, so lag no longer builds up into seconds of input delay or makes the car jump during corrections.
Drift events now run without stability control, which is on by default.
In solo free laps you can now pick any car, locked or unlocked, from the garage. Your choice applies only to free laps, so races, time trials and online play still use your own unlocked cars.

Tournament is now its own solo event with a card of its own, played offline against the AI. It runs four rounds by default and at least two. The other solo events are single races, and rounds no longer hide in the Race event's settings.

The solo tournament now sits on the main menu, and it runs on the game server against AI rivals using your garage car. Rounds are refereed by the server, so tournament races earn XP and levels like online races do.
The Climb and Descent land run is now a sprint, so the road climbs or falls from end to end.

A new Mount Akina course based on the real Gunma route 33 road from the pass above Lake Haruna down the hairpins to Ikaho. It can be run downhill, uphill or alternating, and is picked with a Mount Akina toggle under the New track every race option, which overrides the other track settings.
AI rivals now race in traffic: they pick a side to pass cars they are catching, follow at a safe speed when they cannot pass yet, and keep clear of cars alongside them instead of driving into them.

A new Track style setting: Real, now the default, runs races on 133 real circuits and mountain road sprints, while Classic keeps the old tile tracks. Touch controls and a phone layout are now available for racing. Race circuits no longer draw a centre line.
Remote cars in online rooms now appear closer to where they really are, with less delay and less jitter as they move around the track.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
A new Disaster Race option that adds 22 hazards to the track, with coins to collect and a catch-up bonus for cars that fall behind. A HUD shows the race state during play.
The disaster display now sits below the split plate during races.
Disaster Race mode has a wider camera, a traffic-light start, curbs along the track, fire trails, explosions, a storm, and a new HUD. Rocket turrets and constant turbo are also added.
Disaster Race no longer gives cars a constant turbo boost, so driving feels like the original physics again.
Online rooms show their region and ping in the room list and lobby, and the race HUD shows your live ping. A mixed group's room can now move to a fairer region when a race starts.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

Races now have crashes with damage to five zones of the car, and crashes can leave a car with lost wheels, smoke and fire. Obstacles and hazards are drawn and animated on the track, and lava races have a cracked-crust lava sea with rock causeways. The track picker is searchable, and track settings choose from at least eight circuits.

Replays now show obstacles, lava, car damage, wrecks and explosions, and respawns snap into place instead of flying off. Barrels and mines that go off stay gone for 15 seconds, in both the race and replays.

Cutting across the track no longer resets your car or cancels the lap. Rejoining the road far ahead of where you left it adds a time penalty to your finish time instead, and the penalty is shown in the results. Cars that wreck respawn just behind where they were last on the road.

SCOOP TROUBLE launches as a free co-op pixel-art arcade puzzle game for 1 to 4 players. Ice-cream scoops build and break ice walls to trap enemies and collect every fruit across 120 levels in 12 worlds, played on one keyboard or in online rooms. Online rooms keep your seat after a page reload.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.
Online room links keep their room code when the page updates, so players stay in the same room.
Behind-the-scenes fixes and tidying.

SNACKARANG is a free 3D party brawler for 1 to 6 players, playable on one screen or in online rooms with codes, invite links and a public browser. Snacks throw, curve, recall and slash as boomerangs across 12 arenas with power-up books, bushes to hide in and edges to fall off, with keyboard, gamepad and bot support.
Mouse aim is now supported: the snack faces and steers toward the cursor, left click throws and right click slashes. Mouse buttons only act during a running match.

Stinkwater is a free pixel-art story roguelike in the browser: a year in a fen town as Rax Pu, with seven backgrounds, about 250 branching stories played out where they happen, trades and magic to learn, a real-time dungeon under the old well, and a kingdom that falls and changes around you.

A hotbar of eight slots now holds spells, path moves, tools and food. Pick a slot with the number keys, the mouse wheel or a tap, then use it with F, a right click, the controller trigger or the touch button. A line above the bar says what the selected action will do and to whom before you use it.
TOPOUT is a free competitive block-stacking game with modern mechanics, playable in the browser. It offers online versus multiplayer, CPU battles, replays and a global leaderboard.

The layout now adapts to phones and tablets, with the board filling the screen height on both desktop and mobile. On touch devices, portrait mode shows a rotate-to-landscape prompt until the phone is turned, and touch controls turn on automatically.

On mobile, the game now fits the visible screen, so the browser address bar no longer cuts off the bottom of the board. The first tap on a touch device requests fullscreen, and on Android it locks to landscape. The game can also be added to the home screen as a web app.
Fullscreen works more reliably on touch devices, with a new on-screen fullscreen button and automatic retries on taps until it takes effect.
A back button now sits in the corner on touch screens, so phones no longer need the Esc key to return to the previous screen.

Worlds also generate faster, and the map pans at a corrected speed. Ore now appears in veins at depths that follow the underground layers, with new rock and clay patches, surface lakes, and demonite and crimtane veins in the evil stone.

World generation has been reworked: terrain, caves, ore veins, the ice biome, the Underworld and the dungeon are shaped differently in newly generated worlds.

Floating islands now appear in the sky, with cloud discs, dirt caps, small ponds, sky blobs, and a brick house holding a sky chest. Spider webs are denser, and ruined houses in the underworld are now broken.

The Underworld now has new structures: terraced HellFort towers with doors, platforms, torches, shadow chests and hellforges, and ash towers with horizontal ore veins and lava pockets. Lava also forms flat levels in the underworld, and shadow chests are placed inside the stone there.

Floating islands now sit high in the sky, at least 100 tiles above the terrain below them. The dungeon entrance is now a set of stepped brick stairs instead of a deep shaft, and the dungeon biome only forms where bricks are nearby.

Terrain generation no longer carves caves or places walls above the local surface, so chasms no longer open up near the sky. Trees are now grown after the terrain is finished, so canopies no longer float in the air. Living trees have wider hollow trunks and large rounded crowns.
Trees now grow with more varied shapes, including taller trunks, side branches, roots at the base, and a wider leafy top, with some trees appearing as tall variants.

Trees now have leaf colors that match the corruption, crimson, hallow and jungle biomes. Grass regrows in a late pass after caves are generated, and trees can now grow in the evil and hallow biomes. Weapon damage, knockback and pickaxe power now match the item data.

The on-screen interface now follows a new layout: a hotbar across the top left with blue slots, health and mana shown as hearts and stars at the top right, and a column of buff icons. The minimap has been removed. The inventory opens in a three-column arrangement for crafting, the item grid and equipment, and boss health bars appear at the bottom center.

Inventory now works like a cursor-based pickup: left click picks up, places or swaps items, and right click takes half or places one. The hotbar doubles as the top inventory row, equipment can be moved with the cursor, and there is a trash slot. The minimap is back in the top-right corner, with health and mana shown to its left.
Broadswords now sweep across the whole side you are facing instead of aiming at the cursor. Shortswords thrust toward the cursor and have a more forgiving stab lane, with a longer reach.
The copper shortsword now reaches 2.5 tiles, up from 1.5, so it no longer misses slimes that are right next to you.

Dungeons now generate underground with wandering rooms, winding corridors that widen as they go down, and stairs climbing to a brick entrance tower with crenellations, platforms and a gate. Rooms contain torches, spikes and chests.
Dungeon corridors generate with more varied layouts, and horizontal corridor segments no longer end early.

commits.text: Rebuild Wildbound around a shared Taming-style simulation

updates.summary: Wildbound is rebuilt around one shared simulation, so solo and multiplayer games now follow the same rules. Seasons rotate on a server-wide cycle, with the forest lasting 16 minutes and each of the other five seasons lasting 8 minutes, and each season brings its own resources, wildlife and a stationary boss. Ages now advance on an experience curve, and each age-up lets you pick one upgrade.

commits.text: Predict the player's own tamer online

updates.summary: Your own tamer now moves immediately when you press a direction online, instead of waiting for the server to respond, so movement feels more responsive on a shared world.

commits.text: Spatial biomes, sleeping bosses, food-cost taming and pet levels
Pace ages like the reference footage

updates.summary: The world is now a 3x3 grid of fixed biome squares with forest in the middle, replacing the timed season cycle. Each biome has its own resources, wildlife and a boss that sleeps until someone strikes it, throws thorn rings while awake, and returns 240 seconds after it dies. Aging up is faster: the first age takes a few seconds and later ages about half a minute with kills, gathering gives double xp, and wild kills pay gold.

commits.text: Compact HUD, top-centre age pick and lighter node density

updates.summary: The on-screen HUD is more compact: the leaderboard is smaller, the food, wood and stone counters are smaller while gold is larger, and the XP bar is thinner. The hotbar tiles are slightly larger and the selected slot is dark red. The age pick is now a compact strip of icons at the top centre, and resource nodes appear at a lower density.
